references.name: Corruption Test
references.description: When exposed to a corrupting influence, make the Test chosen by the GM. On a failure, gain Corruption based on the danger; protection, distance, and brief exposure may reduce it.

references.name: Corruption Threshold
references.description: Your sheet tracks a threshold from Toughness Bonus and Willpower Bonus. Reaching it signals a serious consequence: resolve the event with the GM, then reduce or clear Corruption as your table prefers.

references.name: Dark Whispers
references.description: Faint voices offer persuasive but dangerous advice. The character suffers a penalty to concentration when resisting an obvious temptation, but may gain a clue when accepting a meaningful complication.

references.name: Warped Senses
references.description: One sense perceives traces of magic and corruption as colour, scent, sound, or texture. It can reveal the unnatural, though intense manifestations may cause Fatigued or Stunned.

references.name: Unnatural Compulsion
references.description: Choose a narrow ritual, taboo, or fixation. Ignoring it for a scene requires a Cool Test; failure imposes a short-lived penalty until the compulsion is satisfied or overcome.

references.name: Bestial Features
references.description: The character develops conspicuous animal traits. Gain a situational benefit appropriate to the feature, such as keen scent or natural climbing, and a penalty to ordinary social acceptance.

references.name: Chitinous Hide
references.description: Hard plates grow over part of the body. Treat the covered locations as having 1 natural Armour Point, while delicate movement or attempts to conceal the mutation become harder.

references.name: Extra Joint
references.description: A limb bends in an impossible place. Gain an edge when escaping bonds or squeezing through tight spaces, but suffer a penalty when using ordinary armour fitted to that location.

references.name: Luminous Eyes
references.description: The eyes glow in darkness. The character can see in very low light, but the glow makes hiding harder and is difficult to pass off as natural.

references.name: Living Shadow
references.description: The character's shadow moves a heartbeat out of time. It grants a small advantage to intimidation and occult displays, but attentive witnesses can recognise it as unnatural.

references.name: Unnatural Regeneration
references.description: At the end of a quiet scene, recover additional Wounds equal to Toughness Bonus. Fire, sanctified wounds, or another weakness chosen with the GM can suppress this recovery.

references.name: Warp Flare
references.description: Strong emotion releases visible magical energy. Once per session it may illuminate an area or unsettle nearby foes, but doing so immediately draws unwanted attention.

references.name: Crown of Horns
references.description: Horns grow from the skull. They may be used as an improvised close-combat weapon, but normal headgear no longer fits and disguising them requires substantial effort.

references.name: Withered Limb
references.description: One limb becomes weak, twisted, or partly numb. Tests relying on that limb are harder, though pain or effects targeting it may be reduced at the GM's discretion.

references.name: Treating a Mutation
references.description: Mutation is a campaign consequence rather than an ordinary wound. Concealment, dangerous surgery, cleansing rites, and bargains may each help, but every cure should carry a cost or uncertain outcome.

references.name: Public Discovery
references.description: If a visible mutation is recognised, begin with fear, suspicion, or hostility appropriate to the community. Give the character a chance to flee, explain, disguise, or call on trusted allies before escalating.
